def solve_nqueens(n):
    """Solve N-Queens using backtracking with constraint propagation."""
    solution = []
    cols = set()
    diag1 = set()  # row - col
    diag2 = set()  # row + col
    
    def backtrack(row):
        if row == n:
            return True
        for col in range(n):
            if col in cols or (row - col) in diag1 or (row + col) in diag2:
                continue
            cols.add(col)
            diag1.add(row - col)
            diag2.add(row + col)
            solution.append(col)
            if backtrack(row + 1):
                return True
            solution.pop()
            cols.remove(col)
            diag1.remove(row - col)
            diag2.remove(row + col)
        return False
    
    backtrack(0)
    return solution
